citation.authors: Caballero-Purizaga PJ, Arriola-Guillén LE, Watanabe-Kanno GA
citation.title: Efficiency of ODI and APDI of Kim's cephalometric analysis in a Latin American population with skeletal open bite

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 1 difference; logs/task9b2-compare-caballero2019.log). Both values and SDs re-read from the page image of Table 4 (PDF p. 6 = p. 51): ODI 72.10 ± 4.84, APDI 83.18 ± 1.71, balanced group, n 50. The one difference: ODI definitionMatch a 'same' / b 'close'. Re-read p. 48, p. 49 (Fig. 4) and p. 50 (Table 1): the sample-selection FMP (Tweed) uses Go-M (p. 48, Fig. 2), but the ODI itself is Kim's: Table 1 defines the mandibular plane, citing Kim, as a line from the chin along the lower and posterior border of the mandibular body (Kim's tangent wording), and Fig. 4 (captioned as Kim's analysis for ODI and APDI) draws MP from Me as a tangent to the lower border with no gonion marked. So the ODI was measured on Kim's tangent -> same (a). APDI same (both): measured directly as palatal plane to A-B plane (p. 49), geometrically Kim & Vietas' sum. Only the balanced (control) group entered (P19). ageBand 15-40: the stated range of all patients seen (p. 47); the balanced group's own age is given only as 23.66 ± 7.77 y (Table 3). Scale true-size: radiographs calibrated 1:1 (p. 48); both entries are angles, so it does not matter.

caveats: Only the balanced group (n 50; 20 M, 30 F; 23.66 ± 7.77 y) is entered. The three skeletal open bite groups (Class I, II and III, n 50 each; Table 4: ODI 65.87, 67.19, 60.29; APDI 81.78, 73.90, 87.40) are malocclusion groups, not norms, and are not entered.

Balanced-group selection (p. 47): skeletal Class I (ANB 2 ± 2°), mesofacial (FMP 25 ± 4°, Go-Me), USP projection -3 to -5.5 mm, overjet 2.5 ± 2.5 mm, overbite 2.5 ± 2 mm, untreated. ODI and APDI were not selection criteria, but they depend on what was (ODI on the mandibular plane and overbite, APDI on the A-B relation), so their spread is narrower than an unselected sample's (APDI SD 1.71°).
Age band 15-40 is the range of all patients seen (p. 47), not stated separately for the balanced group.
Values are pooled across sexes (no sex split tabled); the regression (Table 6) found sex significant for APDI.
Digital cephalograms, natural head position, lips at rest; values recorded to the nearest 0.5° (pp. 48-49).
The Portuguese abstract gives the balanced APDI as 83,19; Table 4 and the English text give 83.18. Table 4 used.

entries.note: Kim's ODI on Kim's tangent mandibular plane: Table 1 (p. 50) defines the mandibular plane, citing Kim, as a line from the chin along the lower and posterior border of the mandibular body, and Fig. 4 (p. 49) draws it from Me as a tangent to the lower border; the Go-Me plane (p. 48) was used only for the FMP selection criterion. Palatal angle added when PP tilts down-forward (p. 49), as Kim.
Measured directly as the angle between the palatal plane and the A-B plane (p. 49), which is geometrically Kim & Vietas' facial angle ± A-B plane angle ± palatal plane angle (the FH terms cancel).
